newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh's main port still paralysed by strike.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh's main port still paralysed by strike.

text.p: Bangladesh's main Chittagong port was paralysed for a fifth day on Wednesday by a dispute over the use of private equipment to handle cargo.

The deadlock worsened after port users, demanding that the Chittagong Port Authority (CPA) withdraw restrictions on private handling, won a High Court order on Tuesday, officials said. The strike began on Saturday when about 22,000 port workers walked out after Q.C. Shipping Ltd began using its own equipment, as allowed under a recent government privatisation programme.
The workers and their Collective Bargaining Agent oppose the privatisation plan and they forced CPA to withdraw permission. But Q.C. Shipping then asked the court to overturn the CPA ban.
About 25 ships have been stranded at the port since Saturday and 20 others are at the outer anchorage.
Chittagong City Mayor A.B.M Mohiuddin Ahmed Chowdhury on Wednesday asked for a meeting with the port users, including Q.C. Shipping, to try to end the impasse.
The port users have warned the government that a prolonged silence and lack of action against the "trouble makers" might lead to a far worse situation.
Chittagong port handles about 70 percent of Bangladesh's exports and imports, officials said.
